topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: According to the Act's definitions, what characterizes a "designated managing broker"?
choice_a: A managing broker who has supervisory responsibilities for licensees in one or more offices and who has been appointed as such by the sponsoring broker registered with the Department
choice_b: Any broker registered with the Department, regardless of appointment
choice_c: A broker who owns the brokerage firm
choice_d: A licensee who has completed 45 hours of post-license education
explanation: The Act defines a "designated managing broker" as a managing broker with supervisory responsibilities for licensees in one or, in a multi-office company, more than one office, appointed by the sponsoring broker registered with the Department.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under the Act's definition of "escrow moneys," which of the following is explicitly included, without limitation?
choice_a: Commission advances
choice_b: Earnest moneys and security deposits
choice_c: Referral fees
choice_d: Marketing deposits
explanation: "Escrow moneys" is defined to include, without limitation, earnest moneys and security deposits (subject to a stated exception).

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under the "escrow moneys" definition, a security deposit falls outside that definition when:
choice_a: the security deposit is less than $500
choice_b: the tenant has occupied the unit for more than one year
choice_c: the person holding the security deposit is also the sole owner of the property being leased and for which the security deposit is being held
choice_d: the lease term exceeds 12 months
explanation: "Escrow moneys" excludes security deposits in which the person holding the deposit is also the sole owner of the property being leased and for which the deposit is being held.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Per the definition of "escrow moneys," a transaction is considered to exist once:
choice_a: the property has closed
choice_b: earnest money has been deposited
choice_c: the title company has issued a commitment
choice_d: an agreement has been reached and an accepted real estate contract signed or lease agreed to by the parties
explanation: The escrow moneys definition specifies that a transaction exists once an agreement has been reached and an accepted real estate contract signed or lease agreed to by the parties.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under item (6) of the "Broker" definition, a person is engaged in a broker activity when they:
choice_a: supervise the collection, offer, attempt, or agreement to collect rent for the use of real estate
choice_b: pay property taxes on behalf of an owner
choice_c: list a property for sale exclusively
choice_d: manage a homeowners association budget
explanation: Item (6) of the "Broker" definition includes supervising the collection, offer, attempt, or agreement to collect rent for the use of real estate.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-15(a), what is required, in addition to a license, for a person to lawfully act as a managing broker, broker, or residential leasing agent?
choice_a: A surety bond filed with the Department
choice_b: A valid sponsorship registered with the Department
choice_c: Membership in a Department-approved trade association
choice_d: Proof of errors and omissions insurance
explanation: Section 5-15(a) makes it unlawful to act as a managing broker, broker, or residential leasing agent without both a license issued under the Act and a valid sponsorship registered with the Department.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-15(b), a corporation may not be granted a broker license unless:
choice_a: the corporation has been in business for at least 2 years
choice_b: the corporation maintains a minimum net worth
choice_c: every officer of the corporation who actively participates in the corporation's real estate activities holds a license as a managing broker or broker
choice_d: at least one director is a licensed attorney
explanation: Section 5-15(b) requires every officer of a corporation who actively participates in its real estate activities to hold a license as a managing broker or broker.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-15(b), what must a nonparticipating owner or officer of a licensed corporation submit to the Department?
choice_a: A certificate of good standing
choice_b: A fidelity bond
choice_c: A background check from the Illinois State Police
choice_d: An affidavit of nonparticipation as required by the Department
explanation: Section 5-15(b) requires all nonparticipating owners or officers to submit affidavits of nonparticipation as required by the Department.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-15(c), in the case of a registered limited liability partnership (LLP), which partners must hold a license as a managing broker or broker?
choice_a: Every partner in the LLP who actively participates in the LLP's real estate activities
choice_b: Only the managing partner
choice_c: No partners, only employees
choice_d: Only partners with an ownership interest exceeding 50%
explanation: Section 5-15(c) states that every partner in an LLP who actively participates in the LLP's real estate activities must hold a license as a managing broker or broker.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-15(d), a limited liability company may not be granted a broker license unless:
choice_a: the LLC has at least 3 members
choice_b: every member or manager in the LLC who actively participates in the LLC's real estate activities holds a license as a managing broker or broker
choice_c: the LLC is organized exclusively in Illinois
choice_d: the registered agent is a licensed broker
explanation: Section 5-15(d) requires every member or manager of an LLC who actively participates in its real estate activities to hold a license as a managing broker or broker.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-15(f), a license may not be granted to a person, partnership, or business entity if any owner, officer, director, partner, member, or manager:
choice_a: has changed employers more than twice in the past year
choice_b: resides outside the State of Illinois
choice_c: has been denied a real estate license by the Department in the previous 5 years or is otherwise currently barred from real estate practice because of a suspension or revocation
choice_d: has not completed continuing education within the past 2 years
explanation: Section 5-15(f) bars licensure where any owner, officer, director, partner, member, or manager was denied a real estate license in the previous 5 years, or is currently barred due to suspension or revocation.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under the resident-lessee rental referral exemption, a resident lessee referring prospective lessees for compensation must refer no more than how many prospective lessees in any 12-month period to keep the exemption?
explanation: The Section 5-20(10) exemption applies only if the resident lessee refers no more than 3 prospective lessees in any 12-month period.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under the resident-lessee rental referral exemption, the compensation the resident lessee may receive in any 12-month period is capped at:
choice_a: no more than $5,000 or the equivalent of 2 months' rent, whichever is less
choice_b: $1,000 or 1 month's rent, whichever is greater
choice_d: 10% of the annual lease value
explanation: Section 5-20(10) caps compensation at no more than $5,000 or the equivalent of 2 months' rent, whichever is less, in any 12-month period.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: To retain the resident-lessee rental referral exemption, the resident lessee's activities must be limited to referring prospective lessees; the exemption is lost if the resident lessee also:
choice_a: collects a referral fee from the owner
choice_b: shows a residential dwelling unit to a prospective lessee, discusses terms or conditions of leasing with a prospective lessee, or otherwise participates in the negotiation of the leasing of a dwelling unit
choice_c: lives in the same building as the prospective lessee
choice_d: refers prospective lessees to the owner's agent
explanation: Section 5-20(10)(iii) requires that the resident lessee not show a unit, discuss lease terms, or otherwise participate in negotiating the lease, in order to keep the exemption.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-45(a), if a sponsoring broker maintains more than one office within Illinois, the sponsoring broker must notify the Department for:
choice_a: only offices located outside the broker's home county
choice_b: only offices with more than 5 licensees
choice_c: each office other than the sponsoring broker's principal place of business
choice_d: only newly opened offices, not existing ones
explanation: Section 5-45(a) requires the sponsoring broker to notify the Department for each office other than the principal place of business.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-45(a), the name of each branch office must:
choice_a: be entirely unique from the principal office's name
choice_b: include the word "branch" in the title
choice_c: be approved by a vote of all licensees in that office
choice_d: be the same as the sponsoring broker's principal office or clearly delineate the office's relationship with the principal office
explanation: Section 5-45(a) requires the branch office name to match the principal office's name or clearly delineate its relationship with the principal office.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-45(b), for how many offices must a sponsoring broker name a designated managing broker?
choice_a: Each office
choice_b: Only the principal office
choice_c: Only offices with more than 10 employees
choice_d: Only virtual offices
explanation: Section 5-45(b) requires the sponsoring broker to name a designated managing broker for each office, and the sponsoring broker is responsible for supervising all of them.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-45(b), any change in designated managing brokers must be reported to the Department within how many days of the change?
choice_a: 5 days
choice_b: 15 days
choice_c: 10 days
choice_d: 30 days
explanation: Section 5-45(b) requires changes in designated managing brokers to be reported to the Department within 15 days of the change.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-45(b), a sponsoring broker's failure to timely report a change in designated managing brokers subjects the sponsoring broker to:
choice_a: an automatic $500 fine
choice_b: immediate license revocation without hearing
choice_c: discipline under Section 20-20 of the Act
choice_d: mandatory dissolution of the brokerage
explanation: Section 5-45(b) states that failure to report a change in designated managing brokers within 15 days subjects the sponsoring broker to discipline under Section 20-20.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-45(c), within how many hours must a sponsoring broker notify the Department of any opening, closing, or change in location of any office?
choice_a: 48 hours
choice_b: 72 hours
choice_c: 15 days
choice_d: 24 hours
explanation: Section 5-45(c) requires notification to the Department within 24 hours of any opening, closing, or change in location of any office.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-45(d), a record relating to a transaction of a special account must be maintained for a minimum of:
choice_a: 5 years
choice_b: 2 years
choice_c: 3 years
choice_d: 7 years
explanation: Section 5-45(d) requires records relating to a special account transaction to be maintained for a minimum of 5 years.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-45(d), electronic records required to be maintained under the Act must be backed up at least:
choice_a: daily
choice_b: monthly
choice_c: weekly
choice_d: annually
explanation: Section 5-45(d) requires electronic records to be backed up at least monthly.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-45(d), a physical office located within a retail or financial business establishment is permitted only if:
choice_a: it displays a separate sign
choice_b: it obtains a separate business license
choice_c: it is clearly separated from the other business and situated within a distinct area within the establishment
choice_d: the retail business consents in writing
explanation: Section 5-45(d) prohibits an office within a retail or financial establishment unless it is clearly separated from the other business and situated within a distinct area.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-45(e), a nonresident broker licensed by examination or under Section 5-60/5-60.5 need not maintain a definite Illinois office so long as the broker maintains an active license and an office in the broker's other state of licensure, and additionally:
choice_a: pays an annual nonresident fee to the Department
choice_b: obtains a letter of recommendation from an Illinois-licensed broker
choice_c: completes an additional 45 hours of Illinois-specific education
choice_d: files with the Department written statements appointing the Secretary as the broker's agent for service of process and agrees to abide by the Act and submit to Department jurisdiction
explanation: Section 5-45(e)(3) requires the nonresident broker to file written statements appointing the Secretary as agent for service of process and to submit to the Department's jurisdiction.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-45(f), which entity may adopt rules to regulate the operation of virtual offices that do not have a fixed location?
choice_a: The Department
choice_b: The local county recorder
choice_c: The Illinois Real Estate Commission
choice_d: The sponsoring broker's principal office manager
explanation: Section 5-45(f) authorizes the Department to adopt rules regulating virtual offices without a fixed location.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-60.1, on and after what date will applications for licensure based upon reciprocal agreements no longer be accepted?
choice_a: January 1, 2025
choice_b: January 1, 2026
choice_c: January 1, 2028
choice_d: January 1, 2030
explanation: Section 5-60.1 states that on and after January 1, 2026 (the repeal date of Section 5-60), applications based on reciprocal agreements shall not be accepted.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-60.5(a), to qualify for a managing broker's license by endorsement, the applicant must have been actively practicing as a managing broker (or its equivalent) in another state or jurisdiction, immediately prior to application, for a period of not less than:
choice_a: 6 months
choice_b: 1 year
choice_c: 2 years
choice_d: 5 years
explanation: Section 5-60.5(a)(2) requires at least 2 years of active practice as a managing broker (or equivalent) immediately prior to the date of application.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-60.5(a), besides furnishing an official statement from the licensing authority of each state of licensure, what must a managing broker applicant for endorsement also do?
choice_a: complete 90 hours of pre-license coursework
choice_b: pass the full Illinois broker examination
choice_c: obtain sponsorship from two separate Illinois brokers
choice_d: pass a test on Illinois specific real estate brokerage laws and provide proof of successful completion of a Department-approved pre-license endorsement course
explanation: Section 5-60.5(a)(4)-(5) requires passing a test on Illinois-specific real estate brokerage laws and completing a Department-approved pre-license endorsement course.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-60.5(b), a broker applying for licensure by endorsement who has practiced in another state for less than 2 years immediately prior to application must additionally:
choice_a: complete the 45 hours of post-license broker education prescribed in the Act and by rule
choice_b: retake the full pre-license examination
choice_c: obtain a co-signature from a designated managing broker
choice_d: wait an additional 12 months before applying
explanation: Section 5-60.5(b)(5) requires such a broker to complete the 45 hours of post-license broker education prescribed by the Act and by rule.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-60.5(d), prior to issuance of a license to a nonresident managing broker or broker, the applicant must file a written designation appointing whom as agent for service of process?
choice_a: The sponsoring broker
choice_b: The Secretary
choice_c: The county clerk
choice_d: The Illinois Attorney General
explanation: Section 5-60.5(d) requires the nonresident managing broker or broker to appoint the Secretary as agent for service of process before licensure.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 5-60.5(e), the fees required for obtaining a managing broker's or broker's license by endorsement are:
choice_a: double the standard licensing fee
choice_b: waived entirely for the first year
choice_c: the same fees as provided in the Act for obtaining a managing broker's or broker's license in Illinois
choice_d: set independently by each reciprocal state
explanation: Section 5-60.5(e) states the same fees must be paid as provided in the Act for obtaining a managing broker's or broker's license in Illinois.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 10-55(a), a designated managing broker is responsible for the supervision of:
choice_a: only licensees who have not completed post-license education
choice_b: only licensees hired within the past year
choice_c: only unlicensed employees
choice_d: all licensees associated with the designated managing broker's office
explanation: Section 10-55(a) states that a designated managing broker is responsible for the supervision of all licensees associated with the designated managing broker's office.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 10-55(a), which of the following is explicitly listed as a designated managing broker's responsibility?
choice_a: Being responsible for, and supervising, all special accounts of the company
choice_b: Setting commission splits for all licensees
choice_c: Approving all listing prices
choice_d: Negotiating the company's office lease
explanation: Section 10-55(a) provides that the designated managing broker shall be responsible for, and shall supervise, all special accounts of the company.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 10-55(a), in addition to implementing company policies, a designated managing broker's responsibilities include:
choice_a: setting the marketing budget for the office
choice_b: training of licensees and other employees on the company's policies and relevant provisions of the Act, and providing assistance to all licensees in real estate transactions
choice_c: hiring and firing all unlicensed staff without sponsoring broker input
choice_d: auditing competitor brokerages
explanation: Section 10-55(a) lists training of licensees and employees on company policy and the Act, and providing assistance to licensees in transactions, as designated managing broker duties.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 10-55(b), a designated managing broker must directly handle all earnest money, escrows, and contract negotiations for a transaction when:
choice_a: the transaction value exceeds $1,000,000
choice_b: the buyer is unrepresented
choice_c: the designated agent for the transaction has not completed his or her 45 hours of post-license education
choice_d: the property is a commercial listing
explanation: Section 10-55(b) requires the designated managing broker to directly handle earnest money, escrows, and contract negotiations where the designated agent has not completed 45 hours of post-license education.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 10-55(b), licensees who have not completed their 45 hours of post-license education:
choice_a: may bind the sponsoring broker only with the designated managing broker's verbal approval
choice_b: may bind the sponsoring broker on transactions under $250,000
choice_c: must obtain written client waivers before practicing
choice_d: have no authority to bind the sponsoring broker
explanation: Section 10-55(b) states that licensees who have not completed their 45 hours of post-license education have no authority to bind the sponsoring broker.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 20-20(17), absent a legal requirement to pay interest or a specific written request by the principals, a special account holding escrow moneys must be:
choice_a: noninterest bearing
choice_b: interest bearing, with interest paid to the licensee
choice_c: held in the licensee's personal account temporarily
choice_d: converted to a certificate of deposit
explanation: Section 20-20(17) requires the special account to be noninterest bearing unless the character of the deposit requires interest by law or the principals specifically require an interest-bearing account in writing.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 20-20(17)(A), escrow moneys may be disbursed prior to consummation or termination of a transaction pursuant to which of the following?
choice_a: A verbal agreement between the licensee and one principal
choice_b: The written direction of the principals or their duly authorized agents, directions contained in a written contract signed by the principals, or an order of a court of competent jurisdiction
choice_c: The sole discretion of the designated managing broker
choice_d: A majority vote of the brokerage's licensees
explanation: Section 20-20(17)(A) permits pre-consummation disbursement per written direction of the principals, a written contract's terms, or a court order.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 20-20(17)(B), escrow moneys may be deemed abandoned and transferred to the Office of the State Treasurer only if, among other conditions, how much time has elapsed after receipt of a written demand for the escrow moneys from one of the principals?
choice_a: 30 days
choice_b: 90 days
choice_c: 6 months
choice_d: 1 year
explanation: Section 20-20(17)(B)(iii) requires that 6 months have elapsed after receipt of a written demand for the escrow moneys before the funds may be deemed abandoned.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 20-20(18), failure to make available to the Department all escrow records and related documents within how many hours of a request by Department personnel constitutes a violation?
choice_a: 48 hours
choice_b: 72 hours
choice_c: 5 business days
choice_d: 24 hours
explanation: Section 20-20(18) makes it a violation to fail to make escrow records available to the Department within 24 hours of a request by Department personnel.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 20-20(46), which conduct by a designated managing broker constitutes a violation subject to discipline?
choice_a: Failure to provide an appropriate written company policy or failure to perform any of the duties set forth in Section 10-55
choice_b: Failing to attend a continuing education seminar
choice_c: Failing to hold a real estate license for at least 5 years
choice_d: Declining to sponsor a new licensee
explanation: Section 20-20(46) makes it a violation for a designated managing broker to fail to provide an appropriate written company policy or to fail to perform any Section 10-55 duty.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 20-85, recovery from the Real Estate Recovery Fund is available only for a loss of:
choice_a: any type of financial loss, including lost appreciation
choice_b: actual cash money, as opposed to losses in market value
choice_c: emotional distress damages
choice_d: punitive damages
explanation: Section 20-85 limits recovery to a loss of actual cash money, as opposed to losses in market value.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 20-90(a), no action for a judgment that may result in collection from the Real Estate Recovery Fund may be started later than how long after the aggrieved person knew, or through reasonable diligence should have known, of the acts or omissions giving rise to the right of recovery?
choice_a: 1 year
choice_b: 3 years
choice_c: 2 years
choice_d: 5 years
explanation: Section 20-90(a) sets a 2-year limitations period running from when the aggrieved person knew or should have known of the acts or omissions.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 20-90(i), if the Department pays from the Real Estate Recovery Fund toward satisfaction of a judgment against a licensee, what happens to that licensee's license?
choice_a: It is suspended for one year
choice_b: It is placed on probation
choice_c: Nothing happens unless the licensee fails to pay within 90 days
choice_d: It is automatically revoked upon issuance of the post-judgment order authorizing payment from the Fund
explanation: Section 20-90(i) provides that the licensee's license is automatically revoked upon issuance of the post-judgment order authorizing payment from the Real Estate Recovery Fund.

topic: Managing Broker Supervisory Duties & Special Accounts
question: Under Section 20-110, repayment in full of all obligations to the Real Estate Recovery Fund by a licensee:
choice_a: does not nullify or modify the effect of any other disciplinary proceeding brought pursuant to the Act
choice_b: automatically restores the licensee's license without further action
choice_c: permanently bars the Department from further discipline
choice_d: entitles the licensee to a refund of fines paid
explanation: Section 20-110 states that repayment in full of obligations to the Fund does not nullify or modify the effect of any other disciplinary proceeding under the Act.
